 ORDER

These appeals have been filed against the award dated 26.7.2021 passed in Claim Case No.101/2018.
M.A.No.2973/2021 has been filed by the claimant challenging the quantum of compensation and M.A.No.2975/2021 has been filed by the Insurance Company on the ground that it has wrongly been concluded that the insured vehicle was involved in the accident.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 22.12.2017 at around 6.30 in the evening claimant was going by motorcycle from Kanawati to Neemuch.

When he reached near temple at Nimbaheda road,
respondent No.1 came driving vehicle NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35344 2 MA-2973-2021 No.MP-44-TA-0215 rashly and negligently and dashed into the motorcycle of claimant, which caused injuries on the person of appellant.
His D-7, D-8, D-9 vertebra of back bone were fractured.
He was operated upon, plates and screws were inserted.
He also suffered fracture of jaw bone.
He got unconscious due to the accident at the spot itself.
After a prolong treatment although his injuries have healed, but he is now completely bedridden.
He is not able to control nature's call.
He is being constantly attended by someone for answering the same.

sentences.text: The appellant/claimant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the aforesaid injuries.

The Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that it was rash driving of the insured vehicle, which caused accident by displacing the defence raised by the Insurance Company that the FIR was delayed, hence involvement of the vehicle was not proved.

The Tribunal in para 20 to 21 has discussed the issue with respect to involvement of the vehicle and after deciding the same in favour of the claimant, total compensation of Rs.22,83,300/- has been awarded.
3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that a perusal of statement given by the claimant Javed would show that he was making mis- statement before the claims Tribunal.
He has stated that he immediately after the accident has informed about the vehicle, which caused accident.
However, in the medical document it has clearly come that he got unconscious because of the accident.

He also stated in his statement before the Tribunal that he had informed about the vehicle,
which caused accident to his father, whereas he was unconscious, which showed that the claimant was making mis-statement so as to involve the insured vehicle falsely in the claim.

He further submits that after two months of the accident witness Mohd.Ezaz (AW-3) has come out of the blue and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35344 3 MA-2973-2021 has deposed that the accident occurred in his presence, whereas for a period of two months he has neither informed to the Police nor to the family of the claimant.
As such, it is false case of implication of the vehicle in the accident.

4. Responding to the submissions made by learned counsel for the Insurance Company, learned counsel for the claimant submits that in fact the claimant as well as AW-3, both remained firm on their deposition before the Tribunal during the cross-examination.

He points out that statement of AW-3 eye- witness of the accident before the Tribunal was discussed in para 17 of the impugned award in which it has been recorded that the said eye-witness is reliable, nothing has come out from cross-examination of Mohd.Ezaz (AW-3) so as to dispel the statement given by him in examination-in-chief.

Learned counsel for the claimant submits that once the eye-witness was examined before the Tribunal by the claimant and he himself has deposed proving involvement of the insured vehicle the burden was duly discharged by the claimant, then onus had shifted upon the Insurance Company to dispel the same for which the Insurance Company has not taken any steps.
It miserably failed in calling the owner and driver of the insured vehicle.

Not only this he also refers to the findings recorded by the Tribunal in para 19 and submits that the Insurance Company has not even employed its own Investigator and no report has been placed on record so as to disprove involvement of the vehicle.
He, thus submits that the conclusions drawn by the Tribunal in para 10 to 21 of the impugned award are impeccable and does not warrant any interference.

On the aspect of quantum of compensation learned counsel submits that the claimant has asserted before the Tribunal that he was doing the job of painting, thus, the Tribunal erred in treating him as unskilled Labour.
He should have been treated as skilled Labour or at least semi skilled Labour.

He further submits that Tribunal had concluded in para 31 of the award NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35344 4 MA-2973-2021 that the claimant had suffered 100% permanent disability due to traumatic paraplegia.
Once, it was concluded by the Tribunal that the claimant has suffered 100% permanent disability, then compensation for attendant by applying method of multiplier should have been granted.

He further submits that the claims Tribunal should have also The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... vs Javed Hussain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184460354/
2 awarded some amount for loss of amenities and marriage prospects.

sentences.text: Thus, he prays for enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.
6.
From perusal of statement of Mohd.Ezaz (AW-3) as well as the claimant himself AW-1, it is clear that eye-witness Mohd.Ezaz has remained firm in his deposition.
he has also mentioned presence of one more person alongwith him at the time of accident.
The Insurance Company neither employed its Investigator nor made any effort to bring that person or owner/driver of the vehicle before the Tribunal for examination.
Even the Investigating Officer of the Police has not been called for examination.

When the Police has filed charge sheet against owner and driver of the vehicle mentioning involvement of the vehicle in the accident, in such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that burden, which was there on the claimant to prima facie establish involvement of the vehicle in the accident was duly discharged and the onus to dispel the same was shifted on the Insurance Company in which the Insurance Company has failed.
As such, interference in the conclusion as drawn by the Tribunal from para 10 to 21 with respect to involvement of the vehicle is hereby declined.

7. As regards enhancement of compensation, from perusal of the findings recorded by the Tribunal,
it is seen that there is complete absence of any material to show that the claimant was working as Painter.
As such, contention that he should be treated as skilled or semi skilled Labour is hereby discarded.

However, it has to be seen that the Tribunal after elaborate discussion from para 23 to 31 has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35344 5 MA-2973-2021 concluded that the claimant has suffered 100% permanent disability.

Considering the same and in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sidram Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd. , reported in IV(2022) ACC 603 (SC) in para 73 held as under:-
"73.

entities.text: Sidram Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd. , reported in IV(2022) ACC 603 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as this head is concerned, neither the Tribunal nor the High Court thought fit to award anything.
The evidence on record indicates that the appellant is unable to stand, walk, sit or bend his body or lift anything heavy.
It is not in dispute that the appellant will not be able to work in the same manner as he used to prior to the accident.
Indisputably, the appellant has suffered from paraplegia on account of the accident and requires an attendant throughout the day.

According to the claimant,
the cost of keeping the attendant would be Rs.4,500/- per month.
We fix it at Rs.2,000/- per month.
As a result, we award the attendant charges."

8. Considering this, however, in view of the fact that there is complete absence of any material to show that claimant has employed any person as attender the expenses for attender are fixed at Rs.2,000/- per month and by applying multiplier of 18 as applied by the Tribunal for quantifying the loss of earning capacity the amount of compensation for attender comes to Rs.4,32,000/-.
The earlier awarded amount of Rs.10,000/- under this head is hereby deleted.

As regards marriage prospects and amenities of life, considering the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Chaus Taushif Alimiya and another Vs. Memon Mahmmad Umar Anwarbhai and others ,
reported in 2023 ACJ 726 , an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of amenities and further The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... vs Javed Hussain on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184460354/
3 amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of marriage prospects.

sentences.text: As such, total compensation of Rs.5,22,000/- shall be paid to the claimant over and above the already awarded amount alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35344 6 MA-2973-2021 filing of claim application till its payment.

9. The amount, which is enhanced by this Court shall be kept in FDR in any nationalized bank and the amount awarded by the claims Tribunal shall be paid in cash to the claimant on filing appropriate application.

10. In above terms, appeal filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed and the appeal filed by the claimant is allowed in part.
